mstts:express-as.prosody: Have you ever felt that longing—a fleeting sense of wonder that seems to tug at your heart, hinting at something just out of reach? That feeling of joy, both mysterious and unmistakable, weaves through our earliest memories, shaping who we become. Together, let’s step into a story where delight and sorrow, curiosity and doubt, are all threads in the tapestry of growing up. In Surprised by Joy: The Shape of My Early Life by C.S. Lewis, we follow his journey from the innocence of childhood, through the trials of school and the stirrings of spiritual curiosity. You’ll find yourself walking alongside Lewis as he recalls moments with family, friendships that left a mark, and the books that fired up his imagination. Each memory is colored by that persistent ache for joy—a sense that there’s something deeper waiting to be discovered beneath the surface of ordinary life. As we explore the landscapes of early twentieth-century England and the inner world of a questioning mind, you’ll notice how reason and emotion, skepticism and faith, dance together in unexpected ways. Encounters with beauty, loss, and the challenges of belief gradually reveal how longing can shape us, guiding us toward transformation. So, as we begin, let’s be curious. What if the search for meaning—and those flashes of joy—could lead to surprises that change everything? I’m glad you’re here to discover this journey with me.

Chapter 1: Childhood Longing and the First Glimpses of Joy
You know, there’s a kind of memory that just sticks with you—like a flash of something truly beautiful, a feeling that hints there might be more to life than what’s right in front of you. Maybe you’ve felt it too, especially when you were young, when everything was new and every little thing felt full of possibility.
Picture this: a cozy house out in the countryside, filled with books, odd little treasures, and all the gentle chaos that comes with a close-knit family. The boy who lives there isn’t really looking for anything special, but one day, something finds him anyway.
His parents shape the feel of the home in their own ways—one brings warmth and sparks his imagination, while the other holds things together with routines and expectations. Every day has its rhythm: bedtime stories, strolls through the garden, the sound of rain gently tapping on the windows. It’s in these everyday moments that magic sometimes sneaks in.
One ordinary afternoon, the boy is digging through an old box of toys when he finds a biscuit tin—no lid, nothing fancy. But inside? There’s a tiny garden, made from moss and twigs, carefully put together. It’s such a surprise, so unexpectedly perfect, that it nearly takes his breath away. Suddenly, he feels this sharp longing for something he can’t quite name. It’s not just happiness or excitement—it’s deeper, a kind of ache for a world just beyond his reach. Later on, he’ll call it “joy.” And from that moment, it becomes a thread woven through his childhood.
Maybe you’ve had moments like that too—a song, a smell, sunlight streaming through a window—that seem to open a door to somewhere else, just for a second. For this boy, those moments are rare, but unforgettable. They show up out of nowhere and disappear just as fast, leaving him with a mix of wonder and a little bit of loss. He tries to chase them, through stories and daydreams, but they never come when he calls. It’s always a gift—never something he can hold onto.
As time goes on, his imagination becomes a safe haven. He and his brother invent whole worlds together, filled with talking animals, brave heroes, and far-off places. These aren’t just games—they’re a way to reach for that mysterious joy, to keep that sense of wonder alive. Their stories become a secret language, a little world of their own that even grown-ups can’t quite touch.
Of course, childhood isn’t all magic. Loss shows up early, as it does for so many people. The boy’s mother—the heart of the family—gets sick. The routines start to unravel, and a quiet worry settles over everything. When she passes away, it’s like the world shrinks and all the colors fade. That old longing is still there, but now it’s mixed with grief. He starts to realize that joy and sorrow aren’t really opposites—they’re tangled together, and sometimes the things that make life beautiful are also the ones that hurt the most.
Afterward, everything changes. His father, who used to be steady and dependable, drifts away, lost in his own sadness. The boy and his brother are sent off to school, leaving behind the games and stories that once filled their days. Home isn’t a place anymore—it’s just a memory. Still, that longing doesn’t disappear. It’s softer now, but it’s always there, quietly waiting.
Looking back, you can see how these early moments—both joyful and painful—shape the way he sees the world. They plant deep questions that follow him everywhere. What is this longing? Why does it hurt and feel wonderful at the same time? Is there really something—or someone—out there who can fill it? Most people just move on and leave those questions behind. But for a few, the search for answers becomes a journey that lasts a lifetime.

Chapter Two: The Struggle of School and the Growth of the Mind
Leaving home for school—it’s something almost all of us go through, right? But for this boy, that first step into the world beyond his family is honestly overwhelming. Imagine walking into a place ruled by strict rules and even stricter adults. The headmaster? He’s unpredictable, and his authority is absolute. Every day is a blur of lessons, punishments, and this constant, nagging pressure to fit in.
Now, picture being a sensitive, book-loving kid in the middle of all that. He just doesn’t fit with the rougher crowd. The loneliness during these years is almost physical—you can feel it. Sure, he writes letters home, but those words on the page can’t really close the gap he feels inside. So, he turns inward. Books become his escape—myths, fairy tales, histories—anything that lets him step out of the gray routine of school life for a little while. The worlds he finds in stories are so vivid, the characters more real to him than the boys sleeping in the same dormitory.
Most kids, when faced with tough times, find ways to cope. Some get tougher, some just go quiet. But for this boy, the hardship doesn’t make him hard—it deepens his longing for something more. Moments of happiness are rare now, but when they arrive—maybe in a beautiful poem or the description of some distant place—they shine even brighter. The difference between his daily life and his imagination just gets sharper.
Eventually, the school closes, and he’s sent off to another one, this time far from home. It’s a new place, with new problems. The classes are harder. The social rules? Even trickier. He still feels like an outsider, struggling to find where he belongs. But here’s where something starts to shift. A couple of teachers see his potential, and they encourage his love of learning. Latin and Greek open up whole new worlds for him—the ancient stories and philosophies spark his curiosity and give him a sense of purpose.
It’s during these years that the boy starts to question everything he’s always believed. The faith he grew up with? Suddenly, it doesn’t seem so certain anymore. In the classroom, reason and logic are what matter most. He’s drawn to debate, to the clear lines of argument, and bit by bit, he starts seeing religion as something for children—comforting, maybe, but not completely convincing. He still longs for joy, but now there’s a new layer of skepticism.
Even so, friendships—though rare—make a huge difference. One or two classmates share his interests, and together they dive into books and big questions about life. These conversations are a lifeline, proof that he’s not alone in searching for answers. The joy he finds in these discussions is different from the games he played as a child, but just as important.
And looking back, it’s easy to see that the pain and isolation of those school years weren’t wasted. They forced him to think for himself, to challenge easy answers, and to look for truth wherever it might hide. That deep longing for joy didn’t go away—it just changed shape. Now, his search for happiness is tied up with his search for understanding. And honestly, his journey is only getting started.

Chapter 3: The Power of Imagination and the Temptation of Escapism
As adolescence unfolds, imagination can feel like both a safe haven and a bit of a trap.
Picture our young man—he’s caught right in the middle. On one side, reality is always knocking, demanding attention. On the other? Fantasy, with all its comfort and wonder, starts to look more and more tempting.
Maybe you’ve felt that too—the urge to slip into dreams whenever life gets a little too heavy.
His days are split between hard work at his studies and the thrill of invention. Even though he and his brother are miles apart, they keep building their imaginary worlds together, swapping letters and stories.
These aren’t just simple tales—they’re full, living universes, with their own histories, languages, and characters.
And honestly? Creating them is electrifying. There’s something magical about shaping a world just the way you want it.
But here’s something to pay attention to: the more time he spends lost in these fantasies, the harder it gets to stay engaged with real life. He notices that the joy he feels is at its peak when he’s deep inside these imaginary lands.
But try to grab onto that joy, and it slips right through his fingers. It’s real, but it can’t be pinned down or controlled.
Back at school, the pressure to succeed is always there. He throws himself into his studies, eager to prove he’s got what it takes.
Chasing academic success becomes another way to search for fulfillment. And sure, achievements bring a burst of pride—but it never lasts. There’s always the next challenge, the next test, and the whole cycle starts again.
Around this time, he starts bumping into new ideas—thanks to philosophers and poets who see the world differently.
Some say that longing he feels is just a trick of the mind, maybe just a leftover from evolution.
Others suggest it’s a clue, pointing to something real—something that goes beyond what we can see or touch.
He’s pulled between doubt and hope, never quite sure which way to lean.
Meanwhile, friendships grow deeper, and mentors step into his life—people who encourage him to think harder and really question what drives him.
These relationships aren’t always comfortable. Sometimes, they ask him to face truths he’d rather avoid. The pull to escape into fantasy is strong, but these connections keep him anchored.
Late-night talks, sharp debates, and shared laughter remind him that, for all its messiness, real life is worth showing up for.
This tug-of-war between imagination and reality isn’t just his struggle.
So many of us find ourselves stuck between wanting to run away and needing to find our place in the world.
For our young man, the lesson doesn’t come quickly. Over time, though, he realizes that the joy he’s been chasing since he was a boy isn’t found in the worlds he invents—it’s in the longing itself. That ache? It’s like a signpost, pointing him beyond himself, beyond this moment.
As the years roll on, he learns to hold his imagination with a lighter touch. He doesn’t give it up, but he stops letting it run the show. The worlds he creates still matter, but they’re not a stand-in for real life anymore.
The search for joy continues, but now, there’s a new question in the mix: What, if anything, can truly satisfy this longing?

Let's explore Chapter 4: Wrestling with Belief and the Road to Atheism.
When you think about moving from childhood faith to adult skepticism, it’s almost never a straight path, is it? For our young man, this journey unfolds slowly—filled with doubts, disappointments, and that gradual slipping away of certainty. The faith he once held so naturally now feels distant, almost like an artifact from a world he’s simply outgrown.
Those first seeds of doubt take root early. He’s seen suffering up close—the loss of his mother, the sting of loneliness at school—and these experiences spark tough questions. The easy answers from his childhood just don’t hold up anymore. Suddenly, the world looks unpredictable, maybe even harsh. And the idea of a loving, all-powerful presence? It starts to seem less and less believable.
As he moves on to school and then university, he’s introduced to a new kind of authority: the authority of reason. Here, logic, evidence, and a healthy dose of skepticism are celebrated. Religion is often brushed aside—as if it’s just a crutch for people who can’t face life’s tough realities. Wanting to fit in and be taken seriously, he leans into this mindset. He starts to see himself as a rationalist—someone who only trusts what can be seen and proven.
But that shift isn’t without consequences. The deep longing for joy—a feeling that once hinted at something bigger than himself—now feels almost like a cruel joke. If there’s nothing beyond the physical world, maybe that ache is just the brain playing tricks, a longing for something that simply isn’t there. So, he tries to fill the emptiness with other things: chasing success, seeking out pleasure, and piling up intellectual achievements. But none of it really satisfies. The joy he’s after always seems just out of reach.
Throughout it all, friends and mentors leave their mark. Some cheer on his skepticism, making his doubts feel even more real. But others—who aren’t necessarily religious themselves—challenge him to think deeper. They ask those tough questions that make him pause: Why does this longing refuse to go away? Why do the things that stir him most seem to hint at something beyond what we can see? These questions unsettle him, but he pushes them aside, determined to stick with his newfound certainty.
Those years of atheism are marked by a restless energy. On the outside, he’s got it all—great grades, respect, friendships. But deep down, there’s a hollowness he can’t shake. The things that used to make him happy now feel empty. The longing is still there, but instead of feeling like a promise, it’s more like a wound.
Most people, when they hit this kind of emptiness, either try to numb themselves or dig in even deeper to their beliefs. Our young man does a little of both. He throws himself into work, friendships, chasing pleasure—anything to fill the gap. But nothing seems to help. The ache just lingers, a constant reminder that something’s missing.
Looking back, it’s clear this journey through atheism isn’t just driven by ideas—it’s really about the heart. Longing for joy, feeling like an outsider, searching for meaning—these aren’t just puzzles to solve. They’re real parts of life that have to be faced head-on.
What he doesn’t realize yet is that the very questions he’s been running from? They’re the ones that just might lead him home.

Chapter 5. The Slow Return to Faith and the Meaning of Joy.
Change rarely happens overnight, does it? It’s more like a series of small, barely noticeable shifts. For our young man, his journey back to faith moves slowly—almost reluctantly. He doesn’t wake up one morning ready to believe again. In fact, he tries to resist the whole idea. But that longing for joy—the ache that’s been with him since he was a kid—just won’t go away.
The first little cracks in his wall of certainty appear through friendships. Some of his closest friends are thoughtful, honest people—folks whose faith isn’t naive or inherited, but shaped by real struggles and doubts. Watching them, he starts to see things differently. Maybe skepticism isn’t the only road to truth. Maybe reason and faith don’t have to be at war after all.
Books become another turning point. He finds himself drawn to poets and philosophers who wrestle with those big questions about meaning and purpose. These writers don’t brush off the longing for joy; they treat it as something important—maybe even a clue to something more. That idea starts to take hold: what if the ache he feels isn’t just random? What if it’s actually pointing toward something real, something worth chasing?
Of course, it’s not a smooth path. Old habits are tough to break, and he’s careful not to fool himself. Every argument gets picked apart. Every claim gets tested. This journey isn’t just about feelings; it’s as much about thinking things through as it is about the heart. Slowly, he comes to realize that believing doesn’t mean ignoring the facts. Sometimes, it means being open to the possibility that the world is far richer and deeper than we first thought.
Then, almost without noticing, things begin to change. There’s no dramatic revelation, no lightning bolt from the sky. Just a quiet realization: the longing for joy, the sense of not quite belonging, that hunger for purpose—they make more sense as pointers, not just emptiness. He starts to see that the things he loves most—beauty, truth, goodness—aren’t just wishful thinking. They’re hints of a greater reality.
Coming back to faith isn’t about returning to childhood. The big questions are still there, and the journey’s far from finished. But now, he’s not running from his longing anymore. He’s learning to follow it. And that joy he was chasing? It’s never been just about feeling good. It’s a signpost—pointing past himself, past the world he can see, toward the very source of joy.
Most of us, when we look back on life, notice a pattern we never could’ve planned. Those moments of longing, times of doubt, those flashes of happiness—they all weave together into a story. For our young man, the journey isn’t just about finding answers. It’s about becoming someone who’s ready to receive them. In the end, the search for joy turns out to be the search for home.

Chapter 6: The Deepening of Faith and the Challenge of Surrender
There comes a point in every journey when curiosity just isn’t enough anymore. The road ahead begins to ask something deeper—it asks for trust.
For our young man, standing right at the edge of adulthood, faith is shifting. It’s not just an idea to be tossed around or a childhood memory he looks back on. Now, it’s something real, something that actually demands an answer from him. It’s about surrender—not just of the mind, but of the will.
He’s surrounded by friends who, each in their own quiet way, live out a faith that’s both thoughtful and brave. Are their lives perfect? Not at all. But there’s a kind of steadiness about them—a purpose that’s hard to miss. He sees them wrestling with their own doubts, getting hit by disappointments, yet still choosing to believe.
It isn’t blind faith, either. What he witnesses is a hope that sticks around even when the answers don’t show up.
One evening, after a long walk with a friend, the young man really feels the weight of his resistance. He’s spent years building up walls of skepticism, but lately, those walls feel less like safety and more like a prison. That longing for joy, which used to be just a distant ache, is now a steady presence in his life.
It’s almost as if something—or maybe someone—is quietly, but persistently knocking at the door of his heart.
He tries to reason his way out, searching for some loophole that lets him stay in control. But those arguments, once so convincing, now feel thin and flimsy.
He realizes there are mysteries in this world—like the beauty of a sunrise, the ache we feel listening to music, or the pull of a true friendship—that can’t be boxed in by logic alone. These moments point to something bigger than just facts and figures.
Let’s be honest—surrender doesn’t come easily. There are nights spent pacing the floor, silent prayers that sound more like arguments, and long moments wrestling with himself. But bit by bit, almost without realizing it, his defenses start to crumble.
He starts to see that faith isn’t about having every answer. It’s about choosing to trust, even when things don’t make sense. It’s about saying yes to the idea that maybe, just maybe, this longing for joy is a real invitation—not some cruel joke.
Most of us, when we’re faced with the challenge of surrender, hesitate. Letting go of control? That’s tough. Admitting we don’t have it all figured out? Even tougher.
But for our young man, this moment of surrender isn’t some dramatic leap—it’s more like a gentle yielding. A quiet acceptance that he’s not alone, and that the longing he feels points to something true.
Looking back, he can see that this surrender isn’t really the end of his journey. In fact, it’s the start of something new.
The questions are still there, but now they’re held in the light of hope. And that search for joy? It’s no longer a lonely quest. Now, he shares the path with others, walking together toward something real.

Chapter 7: The Integration of Intellect and Belief
For so many people, the real challenge of faith isn't about believing in what we can’t see. It’s about making peace between what we believe and how we think—especially when the world around us seems to divide the two.
Picture the young man, now a university student, standing right at this crossroads. He’s surrounded by sharp minds and even sharper arguments. In academia, skepticism is everywhere—faith often gets written off as nothing more than wishful thinking.
Determined to put his beliefs to the test, he dives deep into his studies. Philosophy, literature, history—they all become arenas where old certainties get challenged, and new perspectives take shape. He’s not looking for easy answers. He honestly wants to know: can his faith stand up to real scrutiny?
Late at night, over coffee or quiet walks, the questions come one after another. Can reason and faith actually live side by side? Is belief just a crutch for those who can’t face reality, or does it answer something real inside us?
The young man listens, debates, and yes, sometimes he doubts. But he also starts to notice something: some of history’s greatest thinkers—poets, philosophers, scientists—they all faced these same questions. And many found faith not despite their intellect, but because of it.
One afternoon, while reading a poem about longing and loss, something clicks. He realizes that the deepest truths often aren’t found in clever arguments, but in raw experience. That longing for joy, that ache for meaning—these aren’t puzzles to solve. They’re mysteries to live out.
Suddenly, it’s clear: faith isn’t the opposite of reason. In fact, it might be its fulfillment. The mind and the heart? They’re not enemies—they’re meant to work together.
Of course, it isn’t a smooth ride. Doubts come back, sometimes stronger than before. And he learns that faith isn’t some steady, uphill climb. It’s a winding path, full of peaks and valleys.
Still, through all the twists and setbacks, he discovers that intellect and belief really can be woven together. Not by ignoring tough questions, but by holding them with humility—and with an open heart.
Most people, when they feel the tension between faith and reason, pick one and leave the other behind. But the young man finds that life is richest in the space where both are honored. The search for joy and the search for truth? Maybe they’re not so far apart after all.

Chapter Eight: The Lasting Impact of Joy.
As the years roll on, our young man finds himself looking at life with a fresh perspective. You know, that old longing for joy—what once felt like an ache or even a wound—has slowly turned into a real strength. It doesn’t just point back to something missing anymore. It actually shines a light on something he's discovered along the way.
He finds himself reflecting on the moments that truly shaped who he is: tending a tiny garden in a biscuit tin, swapping stories late at night with his brother, wrestling through hours of doubt and unanswered questions. Each memory carries both pain and beauty, reminding him—and maybe you too—that joy and sorrow are often two sides of the same coin.
That old longing? It’s not a curse after all. Instead, it's like a gentle invitation, calling him out of himself and toward something bigger.
In his daily life, in his work and his relationships, he’s realized that joy isn’t something you can chase down or hold onto. It comes when you least expect it—a sudden flash of beauty, a genuine moment of connection, or simply that feeling of being at home in the world. He’s learned to welcome those moments with real gratitude, knowing they’re little glimpses of a deeper reality.
Of course, there are still tough days. The longing doesn’t just disappear. But now, it’s wrapped in hope—a sense that this ache isn’t empty, but actually full of promise. He’s started to see that searching for joy isn’t about running away from life, but about learning to see it through new eyes.
Most of us, when we look back at our own lives, start to notice a pattern we never could’ve predicted. The longing, the doubts, those flashes of pure joy—they all weave together into a story that’s uniquely ours.
For our grown man, the journey isn’t just about finding clear answers. It’s about becoming someone who’s ready to receive them. In the end, searching for joy is really searching for home.

Chapter 9: The Shape of a Transformed Life
There’s this quiet transformation that happens when longing finally meets hope. Imagine a grown man who once felt restless, always searching for something more. Now, he finds himself living with a sense of being rooted.
The questions that used to haunt him? Yeah, they’re still hanging around, but they don’t have the same power to shake him up. Instead, they’ve become like companions along the road—a gentle reminder that life’s always going to be bigger than any single answer.
In his everyday routine, he starts noticing meaning in the ordinary things. The laughter shared with friends, the simple beauty of a well-chosen word, the comfort of places that feel like home—these are what keep him grounded.
He learns to spot the sacred right in the middle of daily life, realizing that joy isn’t just for those rare mountaintop moments. It’s actually woven into the fabric of every day, if you know where to look.
When he shares his story with others, it’s never about offering a step-by-step guide. Instead, it’s more like an open invitation. He understands that everyone’s journey looks a little different, and the longing for joy? It shows up in all kinds of ways. Some people find it in art, others in the quiet of nature, and still others through acts of kindness or love.
What really matters isn’t the specific path you take, but just being willing to follow that longing—wherever it might lead you.
Of course, there are setbacks. Old doubts will pop up, disappointments happen, and sometimes that ache of longing returns stronger than ever. But now, he knows these aren’t signs he’s failed. They’re just reminders that he’s still on the journey.
Longing for joy isn’t a problem you have to fix. It’s actually a gift—a way of being drawn deeper into the mystery of life itself.
Most people, when they feel that ache of longing, try to numb it or fill the emptiness with distractions. But the grown man? He’s learned to welcome it, letting that longing guide him back home.
This search for joy, he realizes, is really a search for the source of all joy—the One who gives meaning to every longing and fulfillment to every hope.

Chapter 10. The Invitation to Seek and the Promise of Joy.
Let’s take a moment to think about those times when you’ve felt a deep longing—maybe for something you couldn’t quite put into words.
What if, instead of seeing that ache as a weakness, you could see it as an invitation?
An invitation to look a little closer at what your heart is really searching for.
The truth is, that longing for joy—that sense that there must be more to life—it’s not an accident.
It’s like a quiet whisper, reminding us we’re made for something greater than what this world alone can give.
Our deepest desires? They’re not random. They’re clues pointing us toward a bigger reality.
Of course, the journey isn’t easy.
There aren’t any shortcuts, and nobody gets a guarantee.
But here’s something to hold on to: the promise of joy is real.
Not as something you can grab and keep forever, but as a gift.
And sometimes, it shows up when you least expect it—in those quiet moments of wonder, in the laughter of a friend, or just in the courage to hope for more.
You know, most of us reach the end of a story hoping for everything to be wrapped up neatly.
But if you’ve lived a little, you know the search for joy doesn’t really end.
It’s a journey that keeps going, with a longing that always points beyond itself—a promise that there’s always more out there, waiting to be discovered.
So, what does he encourage us to do?
To follow that longing.
To trust that the ache you feel isn’t empty, but filled with meaning.
Because searching for joy is really searching for home.
And in the end, that home isn’t just a place—it’s a presence.

As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to bring everything together. First, remember—longing for joy isn’t a flaw. It’s something we all share. Think back to those childhood moments that filled you with wonder. Those memories still shape the deepest questions and hopes inside you. Imagination can be both a comfort and a distraction, but it’s also a hint that there’s something real out there, just beyond what we can see. And here’s something powerful—faith and intellect aren’t enemies. They can actually enrich each other, pushing us further than we’d ever go alone. Most of all, that ache of longing you sometimes feel? It isn’t a problem to fix. It’s a signpost pointing you somewhere meaningful. If you ever find yourself haunted by a longing you can’t quite put into words, know this: you’re not alone. This journey isn’t just about one person’s story—it’s about all of us. We each carry a hunger for meaning, a craving for beauty, and a hope that there’s more to life than what’s right in front of us. The path won’t always be straight. The questions might never be fully answered. But searching? That’s always worth it. So, let your longing guide you. Notice those moments that move you—the flashes of joy that break into your everyday life. Don’t shy away from your doubts, or from asking hard questions. They aren’t detours; they’re part of the journey. Trust that the ache you feel isn’t emptiness. It’s actually fullness, just waiting to be discovered. In searching for joy, you’re really searching for home. And that’s a journey worth taking, wherever it leads.
